summary: A 1963 R-6 flat-top built to replace a storm-destroyed neighbor, now storm-damaged itself and closed to rental reservations.

facts.status_note: Damaged by a storm in recent years; recreation.gov listing is closed to reservations until further notice.

staffing.note: NHLR's own page description calls it 'in active service,' but its 2007 and 2015 volunteer visit reports both answer 'Staffed? No,' and the 2015 report describes the structure as trashed and possibly beyond repair.

access.note: Formerly a public Recreation.gov rental; currently closed to reservations until further notice due to storm damage.

visit.trail_note: ~26 miles via North Bank Chetco River Rd / FS Road 1376 from Brookings; rough gravel road, hazardous cattle guard/pothole reported near mile 21.

events.note: Neighboring Long Ridge Lookout, which Quail Prairie replaced, was destroyed in the Columbus Day Storm of October 1962.
Current R-6 flat-top tower built to replace Long Ridge.
Lookout was staffed and observed the Biscuit Fire burning for weeks nearby.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, March 2003 (per brief/register page).
Recreation.gov listing currently shows the facility closed to reservations until further notice, attributed to storm damage per firelookout.com.

evidence.supports: design, active service, and Biscuit Fire observation
evidence.quote: While the giant Biscuit Fire burned for weeks in the summer of 2002, Quail Prairie Lookout saw it all.
The R-6 flattop with live-in cab and catwalk is on a guyed 41' treated timber tower and is in active service.
THIS FACILITY IS CLOSED TO RESERVATIONS UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

evidence.supports: build date and conversion to recreation use
evidence.quote: The tower was completed in 1963 and served as one of the last lookouts built by the southwestern Oregon Forest Service until the mid 1990's, when it was converted for recreational purposes.

evidence.supports: replacement of Long Ridge and storm damage ending rental program
evidence.quote: Built in 1963 to replace the neighboring Long Ridge L.O. which was destroyed in the Columbus Day 1962 hurricane, this 41' treated timber R-6 flat was available on the Recreation Rental program until being damaged by a storm several years ago.
There was a large pot hole abutting the cattle guard. We were traveling at approx. 20 mph when we hit the pothole and cattle guard.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The story had conflated the mid-1990s start of recreational conversion with NHLR registration, but NHLR's own page lists the registration date separately as March 1, 2003; the story now states the two dates separately.

NHLR's lookout-detail description still reads 'is in active service,' but NHLR's own volunteer visit reports from October 2007 and September 2015 both answer 'Staffed? No,' and the 2015 report describes the tower as 'trashed... beyond repair' and asks 'Hard to believe that it was being rented as recently as 2007.' The story now notes this contradiction rather than asserting ongoing fire-watch staffing.

corrections.proposed: restricted — reservations currently closed due to storm damage
corrections.why: Recreation.gov's own listing page states the facility is closed to reservations until further notice, and firelookout.com attributes this to storm damage; the brief's rental.available:true is out of date.

sources.title: Quail Prairie Lookout, Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest

notes_for_editor: Current rental status needs a check closer to publication — recreation.gov shows it closed to reservations 'until further notice' and firelookout.com attributes this to storm damage, but neither gives a date for the storm or an expected reopening. Brief's rental.available=true is likely stale. Fact-check 2026-10-04 found the story had wrongly dated NHLR registration to 'the mid-1990s' (actually March 2003, per NHLR) and had overstated current staffing: NHLR's own 2007/2015 volunteer visit reports say the tower was unstaffed and, by 2015, badly deteriorated. Both fixed in the story and logged above.
